instruction: From the papers listed in references.docx, retrieve their DBLP BibTeX entries (published versions preferred over arXiv) and save exactly 6 entries to 'references.bib', with entries separated by blank lines.

metadata.explanation: Comprehensively verifies references.bib file: (1) exactly 6 BibTeX entries exist, (2) entries are separated by blank lines, (3) entries contain DBLP-specific fields (booktitle, publisher, doi, etc.), (4) entries prefer published versions (@inproceedings, @article) over arXiv sources (@misc), (5) BibTeX entries match papers from references.docx using fuzzy string matching on titles and authors with 0.7+ similarity threshold. Score is weighted: 25% entry count, 15% blank line separation, 15% DBLP indicators, 15% published preference, 30% source document matching (requires 50%+ papers matched with high similarity for meaningful credit).

llm_judge_reasons: IMPROVEMENT: Now uses fuzzy string matching on titles/authors with 0.7+ threshold instead of keyword overlap - this is semantically correct
IMPROVEMENT: Weighted title (70%) + author (30%) similarity matching is appropriate for paper verification
IMPROVEMENT: Source match score now requires 50%+ for meaningful credit, much better than previous 10-30% threshold
CRITICAL FLAW: Match ratio calculation uses len(docx_papers) as denominator (line 344 in getter), but should consider expected_count instead

Logic error scenario: If references.docx has 10 papers but task requires only 6 entries, and agent correctly retrieves 6 matching papers, match_ratio = 6/10 = 0.6, resulting in reduced score despite perfect execution
The evaluator will only give full credit if references.docx contains exactly 6 papers; will penalize correct solutions when docx contains more papers than required
Paper extraction heuristics (lines 88-153 in getter) may be fragile with unconventional docx formatting, could fail to extract papers and cause false negatives
DBLP indicators check (line 307 in getter) only verifies ANY indicator appears ANYWHERE in file, not that all entries have DBLP characteristics
Expected parameter handling is CORRECT: uses expected.get('count') directly as required for type='rule'
Entry count verification works correctly (25% weight)
Blank line separation check works correctly (15% weight)
Published vs arXiv preference check works correctly (15% weight)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix match_ratio calculation in getter (line 344): Change from 'matched_paper_count / max(len(docx_papers), 1)' to 'matched_paper_count / expected_count' or 'matched_paper_count / min(len(docx_papers), expected_count)' to avoid penalizing correct solutions when docx contains more papers than required
Consider making paper extraction more robust: add multiple parsing strategies (bullet points, numbered lists, paragraph-based) with fallbacks
Strengthen DBLP indicators check: verify that majority of entries (e.g., 80%+) contain at least 2-3 DBLP-specific fields, not just checking if any field appears anywhere
Add metadata to track extraction success rate: log how many papers were successfully extracted from docx to help diagnose failures
Consider adding validation that matched_paper_count >= expected_count * 0.8 as a hard requirement for partial credit
